comparator.name: Latin American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: Leiden’s current 2026–27 Study Guide product and public API give 60 EC in each year. This coherent curriculum instantiates the Spanish-language option rather than the Brazil/Portuguese option: first-year Spanish 1 and 2 (20 EC), second-year Spanish 3 (10 EC) together with Spanish-speaking regional subjects (10 EC). The choice reflects the programme’s broader Spanish-speaking Latin American scope, not UCR availability. The remaining first-year foundation is 40 EC of linguistics, Latin American history, literatures and images, languages, Indigeneities and humanities core; second year also has 10 EC compulsory core and a required 30-EC study-abroad semester. Third year has 15 EC compulsory Latin American/world and research-methods work, one first-listed 5-EC restricted choice (Public Policies in Latin America), a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC genuine open elective space. The 0-EC thesis seminar and non-curricular language electives are omitted from the 180-EC component list. The 2026–27 programme-specific OER says no formal graduation tracks and confirms advanced Spanish/Portuguese competence and the required study-abroad and research progression; it notes that a new first year begins in 2026–27. The record represents the complete published 2026–27 structure, not a guarantee about later curricular revisions for the 2026 entry cohort.

exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Latin American Studies bachelor’s defining combination of sustained Latin America-specific history, culture, politics, linguistics, Spanish/Portuguese language progression and study abroad. UCR has no Spanish or Portuguese language course or sequence, and only incidental Latin American examples within broader global courses. Filling 24 places with general history, politics, sociology, media or literature would change the target into general global studies and falsely imply regional and language preparation that UCR does not offer.
exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–27 Leiden curriculum has a 40-EC Latin American/linguistic first-year core plus 20 EC Spanish language, a second year with 10 EC compulsory core, 20 EC Spanish-speaking route content and a mandatory 30-EC study abroad, and a final year with 15 EC compulsory study, a 5-EC restricted choice, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open elective space. Spanish was selected as one internally coherent option; the alternative Brazil/Portuguese option likewise requires sustained region-specific language training. OER Article 2.2 says no formal graduation route, so routeSelection is null despite the study guide’s language-choice groups. The 2026–27 OER introduces a revised first year; later years here are the currently published guide structure and may change for later cohorts.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. The catalogue has Dutch (MCCCOMM112) but no Spanish or Portuguese language course. GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict and GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology cover general comparative or colonial questions, not a sustained Latin American regional curriculum. GOSSOCI311 New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory mentions a Latin American civil-society case, but this is one example in a general global-sociology course. GOSHIST311 Native American Histories focuses on North America, not Latin America. MCCMEDI212 Media & the Environment treats Indigenous and postcolonial media generally. These courses could support selected adjacent questions, but they do not supply three years of Latin American history, culture, politics, language proficiency and the 30-EC abroad component. Their assembly into 24 courses would not be a defensible closest-match programme.
